title: Minimum Operations to Make Array Values Equal to K
statement:
Call an integer `h` *valid* for the integer array `nums`, as it currently stands, when every element larger than `h` has one and the same value (this also holds when no element is larger than `h`).

One operation chooses a valid `h` and lowers every element larger than `h` to exactly `h`. Given a target integer `k`, return how few operations suffice to turn every element of `nums` into `k`, or `-1` when no sequence of operations can do it.
notes:
## Intuition

Operations only ever lower values, so one element below `k` makes the goal impossible. Otherwise, look at the distinct values above `k` from the top down. A valid `h` leaves at most one distinct value above it, so it can be no smaller than the second-largest distinct value: an operation merges the largest value into the next one down (or into `k` at the end) and removes at most one distinct value. Cutting at each next value in turn removes exactly one per step, so the answer is the number of distinct values greater than `k`. A brute force would search over sequences of `h`; a hash set counts the values in one pass instead.

## Approach

1. Walk through `nums` with an empty set `above`.
2. If `num` is below `k`, no operation can raise it: return `-1`.
3. If `num` is above `k`, add it to `above`; copies of a value are stored once.
4. Return `above.size`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [5, 2, 5, 4, 5]`, `k = 2`.

- `5` goes into `above`, which becomes `{5}`.
- `2` equals `k`, so nothing happens.
- The next `5` is already in the set.
- `4` is added: `above = {5, 4}`.
- The last `5` changes nothing.

No value was below 2, so the answer is `above.size = 2`: cut at `h = 4`, then at `h = 2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass with constant-time set operations.
- Space: O(n) in the worst case for the set (at most 100 values here).

## Pitfalls

- Count distinct values, not elements: every copy of the top value drops in the same operation.
- Values equal to `k` need no operation, so they are not counted.
- The `-1` check must see every element; a small value late in the array still makes the goal impossible.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `above` | set of the distinct values greater than `k` |
| `num` | the element being examined |

narration.2: A set stores each value above k only once.
narration.3: Look at every element of nums.
narration.4: Is this element already below the target?
narration.5: Operations only lower values, so it can never reach k: the goal is impossible.
narration.7: A value above k has to be cut down at some point.
narration.8: Record it; all copies of a value fall in the same operation, so the set keeps one.
narration.11: Each operation removes one distinct value from the top, so the answer is how many there are.
